source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Exact source records mapped to established public labels; mapping is recorded for every verse and verified against source KJV annotations. Daniel, Hosea, Joel, Jonah, Micah, and Nahum have chapter-boundary differences.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Preserves both oracle and written vision designations without locating uncertain Elkosh.
verses.before: An oracle concerning Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
verses.after: An oracle concerning Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum of Elkosh.
verses.tsw_comparator: An oracle concerning Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.

verses.rationale: Retains three divine names and repeated vengeance rather than softening the opening.
verses.before: A jealous and avenging God is the LORD; the LORD avenges and is master of wrath. The LORD takes vengeance on adversaries and keeps wrath for enemies.
verses.after: The LORD is a jealous and avenging God; the LORD avenges and is full of wrath. The LORD takes vengeance on his adversaries and reserves wrath for his enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: A jealous and avenging God is the LORD; the LORD avenges and is master of wrath. The LORD takes vengeance on adversaries and keeps wrath for enemies.

verses.rationale: Keeps patience alongside accountability and ancient storm/feet imagery.
verses.before: The LORD is slow to anger and great in power, but the LORD will certainly not leave the guilty unpunished. The LORD's way is in whirlwind and storm, and clouds are the dust of the LORD's feet.
verses.after: The LORD is slow to anger and great in power, but he will certainly not leave guilt unpunished. The LORD’s way is in whirlwind and storm; clouds are the dust of his feet.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is slow to anger and great in power, but the LORD will certainly not leave the guilty unpunished. The LORD's way is in whirlwind and storm, and clouds are the dust of the LORD's feet.

verses.rationale: Retains all waters and three fertile regions with repeated withering.
verses.before: The LORD rebukes the sea and dries it up and makes all the rivers dry. Bashan and Carmel wither, and the blossom of Lebanon withers.
verses.after: He rebukes the sea and dries it up; he makes all the rivers run dry. Bashan and Carmel wither; Lebanon’s blossoms wither.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD rebukes the sea and dries it up and makes all the rivers dry. Bashan and Carmel wither, and the blossom of Lebanon withers.

verses.rationale: Keeps geological disturbance and universal inhabitants rather than reducing to local tremor.
verses.before: Mountains quake before the LORD, and hills melt. The earth heaves before the LORD, the world and everyone who dwell in it.
verses.after: Mountains quake before him, and hills melt away. The earth heaves before him— the world and everyone living in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Mountains quake before the LORD, and hills melt. The earth heaves before the LORD, the world and all who dwell in it.

verses.rationale: Preserves paired questions and liquid fire/rock imagery.
verses.before: Before the LORD's indignation, who can stand? Who can endure the burning of the LORD's anger? The LORD's wrath is poured out like fire, and rocks are broken apart before the LORD.
verses.after: Who can stand before his indignation? Who can endure his burning anger? His fury pours out like fire; rocks break apart before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Before the LORD's indignation, who can stand? Who can endure the burning of the LORD's anger? The LORD's wrath is poured out like fire, and rocks are broken apart before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps relational knows and stronghold rather than flattening into general reassurance.
verses.before: The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble, and knows those who take refuge in the LORD.
verses.after: The LORD is good, a stronghold on the day of distress. He knows those who take refuge in him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble, and knows those who take refuge in the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains feminine unnamed her place and darkness as the pursuing subject.
verses.before: But with an overwhelming flood the LORD will make a complete end of her place, and will pursue enemies into darkness.
verses.after: But with an overwhelming flood he will make a complete end of her place; darkness will pursue his enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: But with an overwhelming flood the LORD will make a complete end of her place, and will pursue enemies into darkness.

verses.rationale: Preserves complete end refrain and ambiguous second-time distress rather than a universal promise of no suffering.
verses.before: What are you plotting against the LORD? The LORD will make a complete end; trouble will not rise a second time.
verses.after: What are you plotting against the LORD? He is making a complete end; distress will not rise a second time.
verses.tsw_comparator: What are you plotting against the LORD? The LORD will make a complete end; trouble will not rise a second time.

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult thorn/drunkenness comparison and complete dryness.
verses.before: For though they are tangled like thorns and soaked as with their drink, they will be consumed like completely dry stubble.
verses.after: Though entangled like thorns and drunk with their drink, they will be consumed like fully dried stubble.
verses.tsw_comparator: For though they are tangled like thorns and soaked as with their drink, they will be consumed like completely dry stubble.

verses.rationale: Leaves the male plotter unnamed and belial descriptive rather than a supernatural proper name.
verses.before: From you came one who plotted evil against the LORD, one who counseled what is worthless.
verses.after: From you came one who plotted evil against the LORD, a counselor of wickedness.
verses.tsw_comparator: From you came one who plotted evil against the LORD, one who counseled what is worthless.

verses.rationale: Keeps enemies' strength and the shift to afflicted feminine addressee, explained in notes.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: “Though they are strong and numerous, even so they will be cut down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, I will afflict you no more.
verses.after: This is what the LORD says: “Though they are at full strength and so numerous, they will be cut down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, I will afflict you no more.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: “Though they are strong and numerous, even so they will be cut down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, I will afflict you no more.

verses.rationale: Preserves male oppressor versus female captive pronouns and physical liberation images.
verses.before: And now I will break their yoke from upon you and tear apart your bonds.”
verses.after: Now I will break his yoke from your neck and tear your bonds apart.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now I will break their yoke from upon you and tear apart your bonds.”

verses.rationale: Marks switch to masculine enemy address and retains lineage, cult objects, and grave judgment.
verses.before: The LORD has commanded concerning you: “No offspring will continue your name. From the house of your gods I will cut off carved image and cast image. I will prepare your grave, for you are contemptible.”
verses.after: The LORD has commanded concerning you: “No more descendants will carry your name. From the house of your gods I will cut off carved and cast images. I will prepare your grave, for you are worthless.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has commanded concerning you: “No offspring will continue your name. From the house of your gods I will cut off carved image and cast image. I will prepare your grave, for you are contemptible.”

verses.rationale: Preserves messenger's feet and explicit Judah addressee, mapping source2:1 correctly.
verses.before: Look upon the mountains— the feet of one bringing good news, proclaiming peace! Celebrate your festivals, O Judah; fulfill your vows. For the worthless one will no longer pass through you; that one is completely cut off.
verses.after: Look, on the mountains, the feet of one bringing good news, announcing peace! Celebrate your festivals, Judah; fulfill your vows. The wicked one will never again pass through you; he is utterly cut off.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look upon the mountains— the feet of one bringing good news, proclaiming peace! Celebrate your festivals, O Judah; fulfill your vows. For the worthless one will no longer pass through you; that one is completely cut off.

verses.rationale: Keeps four urgent defensive commands and scatterer as unnamed attacker.
verses.before: A shatterer has come up against you. Guard the fortress! Watch the road! Strengthen your body! Gather all your strength!
verses.after: A scatterer has come up against you. Guard the fortress! Watch the road! Brace your waist! Gather all your strength!
verses.tsw_comparator: A shatterer has come up against you. Guard the fortress! Watch the road! Strengthen your body! Gather all your strength!

verses.rationale: Preserves like rather than silently and, and repeated plunder plus vine image.
verses.before: For the LORD is restoring the majesty of Jacob as the majesty of Israel, though plunderers have plundered them and ruined their vine branches.
verses.after: For the LORD is restoring Jacob’s splendor, like Israel’s splendor, though plunderers have plundered them and ruined their vine branches.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD is restoring the majesty of Jacob as the majesty of Israel, though plunderers have plundered them and ruined their vine branches.

verses.rationale: Renders two rare equipment terms cautiously with uncertainty noted; retains color and preparation.
verses.before: The shields of the warriors are red; the soldiers are clothed in scarlet. The chariots flash like fire on the day they are prepared, and the cypress spears are brandished.
verses.after: His warriors’ shields are red; his soldiers are clothed in scarlet. The chariots flash with fiery metal on the day he prepares them, and cypress spears are brandished.
verses.tsw_comparator: The shields of the warriors are red; the soldiers are clothed in scarlet. The chariots flash like fire on the day they are prepared, and the cypress spears are brandished.

verses.rationale: Keeps both locations and two rapid light similes.
verses.before: The chariots race wildly through the streets; they rush through the squares. Their appearance is like torches; they dart like lightning.
verses.after: Chariots race wildly through the streets and rush about the squares. They look like torches; they dart like lightning.
verses.tsw_comparator: The chariots race wildly through the streets; they rush through the squares. Their appearance is like torches; they dart like lightning.

verses.rationale: Keeps unnamed commander, stumbling, and uncertain siege screen without fixing attacker/defender identification.
verses.before: He remembers his nobles; they stumble as they advance. They hurry to the wall, and the siege shelter is set in place.
verses.after: He summons his nobles; they stumble as they go. They hurry to her wall, and the protective screen is set in place.
verses.tsw_comparator: He remembers his nobles; they stumble as they advance. They hurry to the wall, and the siege shelter is set in place.

verses.rationale: Retains terse water and dissolution imagery without inventing the engineering of Nineveh's fall.
verses.before: The river gates are opened, and the palace melts away.
verses.after: The river gates are opened; the palace dissolves.
verses.tsw_comparator: The river gates are opened, and the palace melts away.

verses.rationale: Chooses passive decree rather than proper name Huzzab; preserves female captives and mourning gesture.
verses.before: It is decreed: she is stripped and carried away. Her servant women moan like doves, beating upon their hearts.
verses.after: It is decreed: she is exposed and led away. Her slave women moan like doves, beating their breasts.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is decreed: she is stripped and carried away. Her servant women moan like doves, beating upon their hearts.

verses.rationale: Follows difficult since-her-days wording and repeated futile command.
verses.before: Nineveh has been like a pool of water, but now its waters are fleeing. “Stop! Stop!” But no one turns back.
verses.after: Nineveh has been like a pool of water since her earliest days, but now they are fleeing. “Stop! Stop!” No one turns back.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nineveh has been like a pool of water, but now its waters are fleeing. “Stop! Stop!” But no one turns back.

verses.rationale: Retains doubled plunder imperative and abundant loot.
verses.before: Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold! There is no end to the treasure, an abundance of every precious thing.
verses.after: Plunder silver! Plunder gold! There is no end to the treasure, a wealth of every precious object.
verses.tsw_comparator: Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold! There is no end to the treasure, an abundance of every precious thing.

verses.rationale: Uses sound-linked English for three Hebrew devastation words and preserves all bodily reactions.
verses.before: Empty, emptied, and devastated! Hearts melt, knees tremble, anguish is in every body, and every face grows pale.
verses.after: Empty, emptied, devastated! Hearts melt, knees buckle; every waist writhes, and every face loses its color.
verses.tsw_comparator: Empty, emptied, and devastated! Hearts melt, knees tremble, anguish is in every body, and every face grows pale.

verses.rationale: Keeps the whole lion family and ironic lost security without overexplaining royal symbolism in text.
verses.before: Where is the lions' den, the feeding place of the young lions, where lion and lioness walked, and the lion's cub, with no one to make them afraid?
verses.after: Where is the lions’ den, the feeding ground of the young lions, where lion, lioness, and cub walked with no one to frighten them?
verses.tsw_comparator: Where is the lions' den, the feeding place of the young lions, where lion and lioness walked, and the lion's cub, with no one to make them afraid?

verses.rationale: Retains repeated prey and violent provision as the empire image.
verses.before: The lion tore enough for the cubs and strangled prey for the lionesses. The lion filled caves with prey and dens with torn flesh.
verses.after: The lion tore enough prey for his cubs and strangled prey for his lionesses. He filled his lairs with prey, his dens with torn flesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: The lion tore enough for the cubs and strangled prey for the lionesses. The lion filled caves with prey and dens with torn flesh.

verses.rationale: Preserves source her/your shift, lion-to-military linkage, and final silencing of messengers.
verses.before: “Look, I am against you,” says the LORD of Hosts. “I will burn your chariots in smoke, and the sword will devour your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers will be heard no more.”
verses.after: “I am against you,” declares the LORD of Armies. “I will burn her chariots into smoke; the sword will consume your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and your messengers’ voices will be heard no more.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Look, I am against you,” says the LORD of Hosts. “I will burn your chariots in smoke, and the sword will devour your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers will be heard no more.”

comparative_references.scope: All 28 TSW verses bound and compared programmatically after independent drafting from each selected original-language record and all annotations. Selected differences read during focused authoring checks. Overlap is triage only.
